correctness.rationale: For all quadratics the unique critical-level fiber is a singleton. Any cubic with a double critical point is a translated pure cube. For distinct cubic critical points, the integrated normal form factors as (t-u)^2(t+2u) and (t+u)^2(t-2u), and their intervals intersect exactly in the critical segment. For the explicit quartic, direct differentiation gives critical points -8/5 and +/-i. Exact polynomial division gives three factorisations; the rational point 2/21 belongs to each resulting root hull by convex weights 89/112 and 5/14, but has positive real part while all critical points have nonpositive real part. The embedded symbolic checker executes these identities; no computational extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The entire eight-page v1 primary manuscript and its withdrawal notice were inspected. The withdrawn all-shifts identity and the paper's one-shift multiplicity criterion do not imply the finite critical-value sampling threshold. Published mathematical-record searches targeted the exact claim, equivalent fiber and additive-shift formulations, and the source identifier. Closest retrieved findings concern critical-point reciprocal moments, not intersections of critical-level root hulls. Public searches surfaced classical and refined Gauss-Lucas hull containments, but no covering result for the specific finite sampling statement. A differently notated or unindexed equivalent remains possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased argument could establish the same finite critical-value sampling boundary.

The original motivating preprint was withdrawn: no claim about all additive shifts is assumed or asserted as true.

value.rationale: The finite set of critical values is the intrinsic first candidate for replacing an uncountable family of additive shifts in polynomial zero-hull geometry. Complete success through degree three and an exact degree-four obstruction identify the minimal structural failure of this natural shortcut. The witness is a rational point for a rational monic quartic with elementary critical points, and the boundary persists independently of the withdrawn full-shifts proposal. This is a motivated sharp-degree obstruction, not an arbitrary parameter computation.
